Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [smite] the necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and afterwards either [grant] release or ransom until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - He will not waste their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 4]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the group of believers in Him and His Messenger: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, from among the people of war, then strike their necks.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds﴾

He says: until, when you have overpowered them and subdued those among them whose necks you did not strike, so that they become captives in your hands. ﴿Then secure their bonds﴾ means: then bind them in fetters, lest they kill you or flee from you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾

He says: when you have taken them captive after inflicting slaughter, then either you may show favour to them afterwards by releasing them from captivity and freeing them without compensation or ransom, or they may ransom themselves from you by giving you something of their own as a substitute, so that you release them and let them go their way.

The scholars differed concerning His saying: ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾. Some of them said: it is abrogated (mansukh), abrogated by His saying: ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ and His saying: ﴿So if you overtake them in war, then disperse those behind them﴾.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd and Ibn Isa al-Damghani related to us, both saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, that he used to say, concerning His saying: ﴿afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾, that it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

* Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾, he said: it was abrogated by ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾: it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿So if you overtake them in war, then disperse those behind them﴾.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve﴾ up to His saying: ﴿or ransom﴾: The Muslims, when they met the polytheists, would fight them, and when they took a captive from among them, they had no option but to ransom him or show favour to him and then release him. That was abrogated after His saying: ﴿So if you overtake them in war, then disperse those behind them﴾, i.e., admonish by them others among the people, so that perhaps they will remember.

* ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from ʿAbd al-Karim al-Jazari, who said: A captive who had been taken was written to me about to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and it was mentioned that they sought his ransom for such-and-such. Abu Bakr said: Kill him; the killing of a man from the polytheists is dearer to me than such-and-such.

* Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [smite] the necks﴾ ... to the end of the verse, he said: The ransom is abrogated. It was abrogated by: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ ... to ﴿every place of ambush﴾. He said: Thereafter no polytheist retained any covenant or sanctity after the declaration of immunity (Bara'ah) and the passing of the sacred months.

* I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾: this is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. Thereafter no polytheist retained any covenant or protection after the declaration of immunity.

Others said: it is muhkam (decisive), not abrogated, and they said: it is not permissible to kill a captive; rather, it is permissible only to show favour to him or to ransom him.

Those who said that:

* Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu ʿAttab Sahl ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Jaʿfar related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Captives were brought to al-Hajjaj, and he handed a man over to Ibn ʿUmar to kill him. Ibn ʿUmar said: We were not commanded with this. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾. [[Possibly a word or something similar has dropped from the original here, such as "intensified" or "rose", meaning: the weeping of the captives rose before al-Hajjaj.]] Weeping before him. Al-Hasan said: If this man and his companions had been [such people], they would have rushed toward them.

* Ibn Humayd and Ibn Isa al-Damghani related to us, both saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta', that he disliked killing a polytheist in cold blood, and he would recite this verse: ﴿afterwards either [grant] release or ransom﴾.

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Hasan, who said: Captives are not to be killed except in battle, when the enemy is roused against them.

* He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, who said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz would ransom them, a man for a man, and al-Hasan disliked ransoming with wealth.

* He said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from a man of the people of Syria who used to guard ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, and he was from the Banu Asad, who said: I never saw ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, kill a captive except one Turk. Captives from among the Turks were brought, and he ordered that they be enslaved. A man among those who had brought them said: O Commander of the Faithful, if you had seen this one of them killing Muslims, your weeping over them would have increased. ʿUmar said: Then take him and kill him. He stood up to him and killed him.

The correct view in our opinion regarding this is that this verse is muhkam, not abrogated. The characteristic of abrogation and abrogator, as we have explained in other places in our book, is that it is impossible for the two rulings to be combined in one situation, or that proof has been established that one of them abrogates the other. It is not objectionable that the choice between grace, ransom and killing was given to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to those who stand after him in charge of the affairs of the community, even though killing is not mentioned in this verse, because permission to kill them has already been given in another verse, namely His saying: ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ ... the verse. Indeed, that is so, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to act thus toward those from the people of war who became captives in his hand: he would kill some, ransom some, and show favour to some. On the Day of Badr he killed ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt when he had been brought as a captive; he killed the Banu Qurayzah after they had come down under the judgment of Saʿd and had become subject in his hand, while he was able to ransom them or show them favour. He ransomed a group of the polytheist captives who had been taken at Badr, and he showed favour to Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi while he was a captive in his hand. This practice remained established throughout his conduct toward the people of war from the time Allah permitted him to fight them until He took him to Himself, ﷺ. Rather, He, mighty is His praise, mentioned in this verse grace and ransom concerning captives, singling out their mention here, because the command to kill them and the permission for that had been previously repeated in the other verses of His revelation; so He informed His Prophet ﷺ, through what is mentioned in this verse of grace and ransom, of what he had concerning them along with killing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks, and do with their captives what I have explained to you, until the war lays down its sins and the burdens of its people, the polytheists in Allah, by their repenting to Allah from their polytheism, so that they believe in Him and His Messenger, and obey Him in His commands and prohibitions. That is the war laying down its burdens. It has been said: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾ means: until the war casts off the burdens of its people. And it has been said: the meaning of that is: until the one waging war lays down his burdens.

Those of the interpreters said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waqqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾: He said: until ʿIsa son of Maryam comes out, and every Jew and Christian and adherent of a religion submits, and the sheep is safe from the wolf, and a mouse does not gnaw at a bag, and enmity disappears from all things. That is the manifestation of Islam over all religion, and a Muslim man will enjoy such ease that his foot will drip with blood when he sets it down.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾: until there is no polytheism.

* ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾: until there is no polytheism.

Those who said: by "war" in this place is meant the ones waging war.

* ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾: "The war": whoever fights them, he called them war.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That [is the command]. And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: this which I have commanded you, O believers, concerning killing the polytheists when you meet them in war, binding them in fetters after overpowering them and capturing them, and grace and ransom, ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾, is the truth which your Lord has obligated upon you. And if your Lord willed and desired, He would have taken vengeance upon these polytheists against whom this ruling is applied, with a swift punishment from Him, and would have spared you all of that; but He, may His remembrance be exalted, disliked taking vengeance upon them and punishing them swiftly except by your hands, O believers. ﴿But [He ordered fighting] to test some of you by means of others﴾ means: that He may test you by them, so that He knows those of you who strive and endure, and tests them through you, punishing by your hands whomever He wills of them, and admonishing by whomever of them He wills those whom He destroyed by your hands, until he turns back to the truth.

Those of the interpreters said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And if Allah had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them﴾: Yes, by Allah, with His many hosts; every creature of His is a host for Him, and if He had empowered His weakest creature, it would have been a host.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who are killed in the cause of Allah﴾

The readers differed in reciting this. The common readers of the Hijaz and Kufa recited ﴿those who fought (qatalū)﴾ with an alif, meaning: they waged war against the polytheists and struggled against them. al-Hasan al-Basri, as is reported from him, recited ﴿quttilū﴾ with a damma on the qaf and a shadda on the ta', meaning that the polytheists killed them one after another, but the agents were not named. It is reported from al-Jahdari, ʿAsim, that he recited ﴿qatalū﴾ with a fatha on the qaf and a lightened ta', meaning: those whom the polytheists who disbelieve in Allah killed. Abu ʿAmr recited ﴿qutilū﴾ with a damma on the qaf and a lightened ta', meaning: those whom the polytheists killed, then he dropped the agents, leaving the doer of that against them unnamed.

The most correct of the readings in our view is the reading of those who recited ﴿those who fought (qatalū)﴾, due to the agreement of the authorities among the readers, although each of them has understandable aspects.

Since that is the most correct reading in our view, the interpretation of the speech is: those of you who fought, O believers, the enemies of Allah from among the disbelievers, in the religion of Allah, and in support of what His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ was sent with of guidance, and struggled against them in that, ﴿He will not waste their deeds﴾, meaning: Allah will not make the deeds which they did in this world an error against them, as He made the deeds of the disbelievers go astray.

It is reported that this verse is meant concerning the people of Uhud.

Those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And those who are killed in the cause of Allah, He will not waste their deeds﴾: It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed on the day of Uhud, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the ravine, and wounds and killing had spread among them. The polytheists called out that day: "Hubal is exalted!" The Muslims called back: "Allah is higher and more majestic!" The polytheists called: "A day for a day; war is a shared turn; we have al-ʿUzza, and you have no al-ʿUzza!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector. The slain are of different kinds: as for our slain, they are alive and provided for; as for your slain, they are in the Fire, being punished."

* ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And those who are killed in the cause of Allah, He will not waste their deeds﴾: He said: those who were killed on the day of Uhud.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 47, verses 5–7:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs. (5) And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them. (6) O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet. (7)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will grant success in acting in that which pleases and is loved by Him to those who fought in His cause. ﴿And He will set right their affairs﴾, that is, He will put right their situation and condition in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾. He says: Allah will admit them to His Paradise which He has made known, that is, made known and clarified to them, so that a man, when he enters it, comes to his dwelling therein just as he used to come to his dwelling in this world, and that is not confusing to him.

As:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: "When Allah delivers the believers from the Fire, they will be held back at a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and some of them will take retribution from others for the many wrongs that were between them in the world. Then they will be given permission to enter Paradise. He said: The believer will not be better guided to his dwelling in the world than he is to his dwelling in Paradise when he enters it."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾, he said: that is, their dwellings therein.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾, he said: its people will be guided to their houses and dwellings, and to where Allah has allotted them, they will not err, as if they had been its inhabitants since they were created, not needing to ask anyone about it.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾, he said: We have been told by more than one person: The people of Paradise will enter Paradise, and they will know their dwellings therein better than they knew their dwellings in the world, which they used to visit throughout the length of the world's life. He said: That is the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, if you support Allah, He will support you by your supporting His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) against his enemies from among the people of disbelief in Him, and by your striving against them alongside him, so that His word may be supreme; He will support you against them and grant you victory over them, for He is the supporter of His religion and His allies.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿if you support Allah, He will support you﴾, he said: because it is incumbent upon Allah to give to the one who asks Him and to support the one who supports Him.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and plant firmly your feet﴾

He says: He will strengthen you against them and embolden you, so that you do not turn your backs to them, even if their number is great and your number is small.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 47, verses 5–7:

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs. (5) And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them. (6) O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet. (7)﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, will grant success in acting in that which pleases and is loved by Him to those who fought in His cause. ﴿And He will set right their affairs﴾, that is, He will put right their situation and condition in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾. That is, He made their deeds performed without guidance or uprightness, because they were done in obedience to Satan, not in obedience to the Most Merciful.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and He will waste their deeds﴾: "The misguidance with which Allah misguided them is that He did not guide them as He guided others, for the misguidance of which Allah informs you is: He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills." He said: "These are among those whose deeds He made into error, and He referred the words ﴿and He will waste their deeds﴾ back to His words ﴿for them is ruin﴾, which is a past-tense verb, while ta's (ruin) is a noun. Although ta's is a noun, it carries the meaning of a verb because it contains the sense of supplication, so it means: 'May Allah bring them to ruin.' Therefore it is valid to refer adalla back to it, since supplication takes the place of command and prohibition. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 10:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land, so that they might see how was the end of those before them? God destroyed them utterly, and for the disbelievers there are the like of these.﴾

Say: Exalted is His remembrance. Did these deniers not travel in the land, so as to see? This is a rebuke from God to them, for they used to travel to Syria and would see the vengeance of God which He brought upon the people of al-Hijr of Thamud, and on their journey to Yemen they would see what God brought upon Saba'. So He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in him: Have these polytheists not travelled in the lands, so that they might see how was the end of the denial of those who came before them, of the nations who denied their messengers and rejected their admonitions? Did We not destroy them, and so We razed their dwellings and laid them waste? Let them take warning from that, and beware lest God do to them the same for their denial of Him, so that they turn back in obedience to God by believing you. Then He threatened them, exalted is His praise, and informed them that if they persisted in denying His Messenger, He would bring upon them the punishment that He had brought upon the nations before them. So He said: ﴿And for the disbelievers there are the like of these﴾, meaning: And for the disbelievers among the Quraysh who deny the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there are a hastened punishment like the end of the nations before them who denied their messengers for denying His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And how many a town, O Muhammad, was mightier in strength than your town, meaning its people were mightier in might, more numerous in gathering, and greater in number than the people of your town, which is Makkah. Then He said: "have We destroyed them," because the meaning in His saying "has driven you out" is what I described, that what is meant is the people of the town. So He related the report once according to the wording and once according to the meaning.

As for His saying ﴿so there was none to help them﴾

There are two interpretations of it. The first is that its meaning is: even though "the helper" (al-nasir) was put in the accusative by the negation of the category (al-tabri'ah), there was no helper for them. This is because the Arabs sometimes omit "kana" (was) in such constructions. The second is that its meaning is: so there is now no helper for them to save them from the punishment of Allah.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive, and who follow their desires?﴾ (47:14)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Is he who is﴾ upon proof, argument and clarification ﴿from﴾ the affair of ﴿his Lord﴾ and knowledge of His oneness, so that he worships Him with insight from Him, knowing that he has a Lord who will reward him with Paradise for his obedience to Him, and with the Fire for his disobedience and sin against Him, ﴿like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive﴾, meaning: like one for whom Satan has made his ugly and evil deeds seem good, showing them to him as beautiful, so that he remains persistent in acting upon them, ﴿and who follow their desires﴾, meaning: and who follow what their souls have called them to of disobedience to God and worship of idols, without having any proof or argument for what they do of that. It has been said that what is meant by His saying, ﴿Is he who is upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾ is our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and that what is meant by His saying, ﴿like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive﴾ is the polytheists.

The Interpretation of His, the Exalted's, Words: ﴿The parable of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised: therein are rivers of water unchanging, and rivers of milk whose taste does not alter, and rivers of wine, a delight to the drinkers, and rivers of clarified honey; and for them therein is every kind of fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord. Is this like one who abides in the Fire, and is given to drink boiling water which tears apart their bowels?﴾ (15)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: this is the description of the Garden which was promised to the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), those who in this world guarded themselves against His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿Therein are rivers of water unchanging (ghayr asin)﴾ — He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: in this Garden which He has mentioned are rivers of water whose smell does not change. It is said of it: the water of this well has become asin (ʾasana, "to become foul/changed") when the smell of its water has changed and become putrid; so it is yaʾsinu asanan. Likewise it is said of a man when a foul odour afflicts him: he has become asin, and he is yaʾsanu. But when water becomes stagnant and changes, it is said of it: asin, yaʾsanu, yaʾsinu ʾusunan, and it is ma' asin.

In line with what we have said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿water unchanging (ghayr asin)﴾, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

He said: It has reached me that no hand touches it, and that the water comes thus until it enters into its mouth.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: therein are rivers of milk whose taste has not altered, because it was not milked from an animal whose taste would change by leaving the udders; rather, Allah created it from the beginning in the rivers, so in its form it has not changed from how He created it.

- Isa related to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Musab related to us, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, who said: I asked al-Harith about it, and he said: The Magians have not trodden it, nor has Satan breathed into it, nor has the sun harmed it, but it is fawha' [[In al-Lisan: al-fawh: finding a pleasant scent. The fragrance of musk wafts (yafuhu and yafihu), fawhan and fayhan; and fawhanan fayhanan: its scent spread.]]. He said: I said to Ikrima: What is al-fawha'? He said: The yellow.

And as:

And "delight" (ladhdha) is in the genitive as an attribute of the wine. If it had come in the nominative as an attribute of the rivers, it would be permissible; or in the accusative, as "they take pleasure in it with pleasure," as one says "this is a gift to you," it would be permissible. But as for the recitation, I do not permit it except in the genitive, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters is upon it.

He says: therein are rivers of honey which has been clarified of impurities. * *

As for His words ﴿and for them therein is every kind of fruit﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: for these God-fearing ones in this Garden, from these rivers which we have mentioned, is every kind of fruit that grows on trees. ﴿And forgiveness from their Lord﴾ — he says: and pardon from Allah for them regarding their sins which they committed in this world, then repented of, and a pardoning from Him of punishment for them.

* *

As for His words ﴿Is this like one who abides in the Fire﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Is the one who is in this Garden, whose description is what we have described, like one who abides in the Fire? The speech began with the description of the Garden, so it was said: the parable of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised, and it did not say: Is he who is in the Garden [like...]. Then, after finishing the report about the Garden and its description, it was said ﴿Is this like one who abides in the Fire﴾. It was said thus because the listener already knows the meaning of the speech, and because His words ﴿like one who abides in the Fire﴾ indicate the meaning of His words ﴿the parable of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿and given to drink boiling water﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who are abiding in the Fire are given to drink water whose heat has reached its extreme, so that water, because of its intense heat, cuts their bowels.

As:

- Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani related to me, saying: Hayway ibn Shurayh al-Himsi related to us, saying: Baqiyya related to us, from Safwan ibn Amr, who said: Ubayd Allah ibn Bishr related to me, from Abu Umama al-Bahili, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿and he is given to drink pus-water, which he gulps﴾, he said: it is brought near to him and he dislikes it; when it is brought close to him, it scorches his face and the skin of his head falls off; when he drinks it, it cuts his bowels until it comes out from his posterior. He said: Allah says ﴿and they are given to drink boiling water, so it cuts their bowels﴾, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says ﴿it scalds the faces; wretched is the drink, and evil the resting-place﴾.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed over their hearts, and they follow their own desires.﴾

Exalted is He, says: And among these disbelievers, O Muhammad, is the one ﴿who listens to you﴾, and he is the hypocrite. He listens to what you say but does not comprehend or understand it, out of contempt for what you recite to him from the Book of your Lord, and heedlessness of what you say and what you call him to of faith. ﴿Until, when they leave your presence﴾, they say, informing those present with them in your assembly from among the people of knowledge of the Book of Allah, and of your recitation to them of what you recited and your speaking to them of what you spoke, that they had not lent their ears to your words and recitation: ﴿"What did he just say?" ﴾ to us, Muhammad? ﴿Just now﴾? And the people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence﴾: These are the hypocrites. Two men entered: a man who understood from Allah and benefited from what he heard, and a man who did not understand from Allah and did not benefit from what he heard. It used to be said: people are of three kinds: the listener who acts, the listener who is heedless, and the listener who abandons.

Qatadah, from Ma'mar, regarding ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾, said: They are the hypocrites. And it used to be said: people are of three kinds: the listener who acts, the listener who is heedless, and the listener who abandons.

Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾, said: I am among them, and I was asked among those who were asked.

Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence﴾ ... to the end of the verse, said: These are the hypocrites, and those who were given knowledge are the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

And His saying ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed over their hearts﴾

Exalted is He, says: These people with these characteristics are the folk whom Allah has sealed over their hearts, so they are not guided to the truth with which Allah sent His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, ﴿and follow their desires﴾, meaning: they have rejected the command of Allah and followed what their souls have called them to. So they do not return from what they are upon to any reality or proof. Exalted is His praise, He equated the attribute of these hypocrites with that of the polytheists, in that all of them, in their departure from the religion of Allah with which He sent Muhammad ﷺ, follow their desires. He said about these hypocrites: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has sealed over their hearts, and they follow their desires﴾, and He said about the people of disbelief in Him from among the polytheists: ﴿Is one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive and who follows his desires [like one guided]?﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verses 17–18:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their taqwa (God-consciousness).﴾ (17) ﴿Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come. So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾ (18)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As for those whom Allah guided to follow the truth, and expanded their breasts to believe in it and in His Messenger, from among those who listened to you, O Muhammad, then what I recited to them and they heard from you ﴿increases them in guidance﴾: meaning, Allah increases them by that in faith beyond their faith, and in clarification of the reality of what I brought them from Allah, beyond the clarity they already had. It has been mentioned that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an to them, the hypocrites among them said to the believers, "What did he just say?" And Allah increased the people of guidance among them in guidance. Some of what Allah sent down of the Qur'an abrogated some of what had been ruled earlier.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their taqwa﴾: He said: When Allah sent down the Qur'an, they believed in it, and that was guidance. Then when the abrogating and the abrogated were made clear, He increased them in guidance.

* *

And His saying ﴿and grants them their taqwa﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah bestowed upon these guided ones their taqwa, and that is His making them act by their taqwa.

* *

And His saying ﴿Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Are these deniers of Allah's signs, from among the people of disbelief and hypocrisy, waiting for anything but the Hour, at which Allah promised to His creation to resurrect them from their graves alive, that it come upon them unexpectedly, without their perceiving its coming? The meaning: Are they waiting for anything but the Hour; are they waiting for anything but that it come upon them suddenly. The "an" in His saying ﴿illa an﴾ is in a place of accusative by way of substitution for "the Hour," and with the alif of ﴿an ta'tiyahum﴾ opened, and ﴿ta'tiyahum﴾ in the accusative by it, is the reading of the people of Kufa.

* It has been related to me from al-Farra', who said: Abu Ja'far al-Ru'asi told me, saying: I said to Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala': What is this fa' in His saying ﴿fa-qad ja'a ashratuha﴾? He said: It is the response of the conditional. I said: Indeed, "in ta'tihim" [if it comes to them]. He said: "God forbid, it is only 'in ta'tihim'." Al-Farra' said: I thought he had taken it from the people of Mecca, because he read it so. Al-Farra' said: It is also found in some of the Kufan codices, with one sunna (a single dot/mark), "ta'tihim," but none of them read it that way.

The interpretation of the speech according to the reading of one who recites it with the kasra of the alif of "in" and the jazm of "ta'tihim" is: "Are they waiting for anything but the Hour?" So the report about the waiting of these disbelievers for the Hour ends at His saying ﴿but the Hour﴾; then the speech begins anew, saying: "If the Hour comes upon them suddenly, its signs have already come," so the fa' in His saying ﴿fa-qad ja'a﴾ is the response of the conditional.

* *

And His saying ﴿fa-qad ja'a ashratuha﴾

He says: These disbelievers in Allah have already been visited by the Hour, its proofs and its precursors. The singular of ashrat is shart, as Jarir said:

You see the shart of the goats as their wives' dowries, and among the shart of goats there are dowries for them.[[The verse is by Jarir ibn al-Khatafi, the Islamic poet (his Diwan, 226); in another narration: "and in the qazam of goats there are dowries for them." It is among the witnesses cited by Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 223), who said at His saying "fa-qad ja'a ashratuha": its signs. The shart were so named, as we see it, because they made themselves known. The ashrat of wealth are small goats and their worthless ones. Jarir said: "You see the shart..." In (Lisan al-'Arab: sh-r-t): al-shart (with vowelling) are the base ones of a single, a plural, and the masculine and feminine are the same in that. Jarir said: "Driven from the goats as dowries for their women, and from the shart of goats for them are dowries." And shart al-nas: their dregs.]]

It is narrated also as: "You see the qazam of goats." It is said of it: Ashrata fulan nafsahu, when he marked himself with a sign, as Aws ibn Hajar said:

So he marked himself therein, while he was holding fast, and cast down his ropes and relied upon Him.[[The verse is by Aws ibn Hajar (Lisan al-'Arab: sh-r-t). al-Asma'i said: The ashrat of the Hour are its signs. He said: From it comes al-ishtirat, which people stipulate among one another, i.e., they are signs they set between them. For this they were called shurta, because they made for themselves a sign by which they were known. Al-Khattabi related from some linguists that he rejected this explanation and said: The ashrat of the Hour are what people find strange of its minor matters before the Hour arises. The shurta of the sultan are the chosen companions whom he places ahead of others among his soldiers. Aws ibn Hajar's words "fa-ashrata fiha... the verse" mean he made himself a banner for this matter.]]

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿fa-qad ja'a ashratuha﴾: He means the signs of the Hour.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly?﴾: The Hour has drawn near, and the leisure of the servants from Allah has drawn near.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿fa-qad ja'a ashratuha﴾: Its ashrat are its signs.

* *

And His saying ﴿So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: By what means will these deniers of Allah's signs have a reminder of what they neglected and squandered of obedience to Allah when the Hour comes to them? He says: That is not a time when remembrance and regret will benefit them, for it is a time of recompense, not a time of seeking to make amends or of acting.

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾: He says: When the Hour comes to them, how can they remember, recognize, and understand?

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?" He said: How can they remember or repent when the Hour comes to them?

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾: He said: The Hour; their reminder will not benefit them at the Hour. The dhikra is in the nominative place by His saying ﴿fa-anna lahum﴾, because the interpretation of the speech is: "So how for them is their reminder when the Hour comes to them?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 19:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement and your resting place.﴾ (19)

His saying, the Exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Know, O Muhammad, that there is no one worthy of worship, or fit to be called divinity, and it is permissible for you and for creation to worship, except Allah, who is the Creator of creation and the Owner of everything, to whom everything other than Him submits in lordship. (ﷺ) And ask your Lord for forgiveness of your past and present sins, and of the sins of the believing men and women among those who believe in you. ﴿And Allah knows your movement and your resting place﴾ means: Indeed Allah knows your movements, in what you move about in your waking hours of deeds, and your resting place when you lie down in your beds at night; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of it.

And Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abdullah ibn Sarjis, who said: "I ate with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I said: 'May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah.' A man from the people said: 'Shall I ask forgiveness for you, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, and for you too,' then he recited ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verses 20–21:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?" But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one who has fainted at the approach of death. So woe to them! Obedience and right speech. And when the matter is resolved upon, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them.﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: "And those who believe, meaning those who affirm Allah and His Messenger, say: Why has there not been sent down a surah from Allah commanding us to fight the enemies of Allah among the disbelievers? ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down﴾ — meaning: one that is clear in its explanation and its obligations." It is reported that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it is ﴿a new surah is sent down﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿and fighting is mentioned therein﴾:

He says: and the command to fight the polytheists is mentioned in it.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "And those who believe say, 'Why has a surah not been sent down?' But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein," he said: "Every surah in which jihad is mentioned is decisive, and it is the hardest of the Qur'an upon the hypocrites."

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding "and fighting is mentioned therein," he said: "Every surah in which fighting is mentioned is decisive."

* *

As for His words ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾:

He says: you see those in whose hearts there is doubt about the religion of Allah and weakness, ﴿looking at you﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿with the look of one who has fainted at the approach of death﴾, out of fear that you would send them out to fight and command them to strive alongside the Muslims. So they, out of fear of that and cowardice in meeting the enemy, look at you with the look of one who has fainted, who has been struck down. He only meant by His words ﴿at the approach of death﴾ fear of death, and this was the behaviour of the people of hypocrisy.

Like what:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿looking at you with the look of one who has fainted at the approach of death﴾: "These are the hypocrites whose hearts Allah has sealed, so they do not comprehend what the Prophet (ﷺ) says."

* *

As for His words ﴿So woe to them﴾:

He, may He be remembered, says: So woe to those whose hearts are diseased.

* *

As for His words ﴿So woe to them﴾:

It is a threat with which Allah threatened these hypocrites.

As:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So woe to them﴾, he said: "This is a threat: woe to them." Then the speech ended, and he said: ﴿Obedience and right speech.﴾

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So woe to them﴾, he said: "A threat, as you hear."

* *

As for His words ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾:

This is a report from Allah, may He be remembered, about the speech of these hypocrites before a decisive surah was sent down, in which fighting is mentioned; and that when it was said to them, "Indeed Allah has obligated jihad upon you," they said, "We hear and obey." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said to them: ﴿But when a surah is sent down﴾ and fighting is made obligatory upon them therein, it was hard upon them and they disliked it. ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾ was said before the obligation was due upon you; but when the matter is resolved upon, you disliked it and it was hard upon you.

* *

As for His words ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾:

It is in the nominative case, governed by an implied element, which is your saying before the revelation of the obligation of fighting: ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾.

It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, through a chain that is not approved, that he said: Allah said ﴿So woe to them﴾, then He said to those among them who believed: ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾. According to this view, the threat is complete with "So woe to them," and then it resumes, and it is said to them: ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾, so that "obedience" is in the nominative as the subject of the implied "for them" (lahum).

Mujahid used to say concerning this, as follows:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Obedience and right speech﴾, he said: "Allah commanded the hypocrites with that."

* *

As for His words ﴿But when the matter is resolved upon﴾:

He says: when fighting became obligatory and the command of Allah came with its obligation, you disliked it.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said concerning this.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So would you, if you turned away, do corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ (22) ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He has deafened them and blinded their vision.﴾ (23)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, concerning those whom He described as, when a clear (muhkamah) surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned in it, looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the look of one who has fainted from death. ﴿So would you (fahal 'asaytum)﴾ O people, meaning: perhaps you, if you turn away from the revelation of Allah, may He be exalted, and depart from the rulings of His Book, and turn your backs on Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought you, ﴿that you would do corruption in the land﴾, meaning: that you would disobey Allah in the land, so that you disbelieve in Him and shed blood therein, ﴿and sever your ties of kinship﴾, and return to what you were upon in your jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) of dispersion and division, after Allah had united you through Islam and joined your hearts by it.

And in the same sense as what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, ﴿So would you, if you turned away...﴾ to the end of the verse. He says: So would you, how did you see the people when they turned away from the Book of Allah? Did they not shed forbidden blood, sever ties of kinship, and disobey the Most Merciful?

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿So would you, if you turned away, do corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship﴾, he said: They did.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, both saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi al-Muzarrad al-Madini narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah created the creation, and when He had finished with them, the womb (rahim) clung to the loins of the Most Merciful. He said, 'Enough!' It said, 'This is the station of one who seeks refuge in You from severance.' He said, 'Are you not pleased that I join whoever joins you, and sever whoever severs you?' It said, 'Yes.' He said, 'That is yours.'"

Sulayman said in his narration: Abu Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish, ﴿So would you, if you turned away, do corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship﴾. Some have interpreted it: "So would you, if you were given charge of the affairs of people, do corruption in the land," in the sense of governance (wilayah). The readers, other than Nafi', were unanimous on opening the sin in "'asaytum", while Nafi' used to pronounce it with a kasrah, "'asiytum".

The correct view for us is the reading with a fatha on the sin, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, and because it has not been heard in speech: "'asiya akhuka yaqum" with a kasrah on the sin and a fatha on the ya'; and if the kasrah were correct, it would come with a pronoun-suffix, and it came with a kasrah with a non-pronoun. Their consensus on opening it with an apparent noun is clear evidence that it is likewise with a pronoun. The "in" that follows "'asaytum" is kasrah, and it is a conditional particle, and the "an" with "tufsidu" is in a position of accusative governed by "'asaytum".

He says: God extended for them their terms of life for a long period of time. The meaning of the statement is: Satan enticed them, and God prolonged for them.

The reciters differed in the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Kufa read ﴿wa-amla lahum﴾ with a fatha on the alif, meaning: and God prolonged for them. Some of the people of Madina and Basra read ﴿wa-umliya lahum﴾ in the passive form, the subject unnamed. As narrated:

The commentary on the Exalted saying: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds﴾ (33) ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – Allah will not forgive them﴾ (34).

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ in their commands and their prohibitions, ﴿and do not invalidate your deeds﴾. He means: do not render void the reward of your deeds through your disobedience to them both and your disbelief in your Lord, for disbelief in Allah nullifies the good deeds that preceded it.

Commentators have said the like of what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds﴾ ... the verse: "Whoever among you is able not to invalidate a good deed by an evil deed, let him do so, and there is no power except by Allah. For good abrogates evil, and evil abrogates good, and the criterion of deeds is their endings."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 35:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you, and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾ (35).

He, the Exalted, says: Do not be feeble, O believers in Allah, in striving against the polytheists, and do not be cowardly in fighting them.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿do not weaken﴾, he said: Do not be feeble.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿do not weaken﴾: Do not be weak, you.

* *

And His saying ﴿and call to peace while you are the superior﴾

It means: Do not be feeble towards them and call them to reconciliation and peace, while you are the ones who prevail over them and are high above them. ﴿And Allah is with you﴾ means: and Allah is with you by granting you victory over them.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said, but they differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿while you are the superior﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: while you are more deserving of Allah than they are. Others said: it is like what we have said.

Mention of those who said that the meaning of His saying ﴿while you are the superior﴾ is: you are more deserving of Allah than they are.

Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father narrate, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾, he said: That is, do not be the first of the two groups to be struck down.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾, he said: Do not be the first of the two groups to be struck down by its companion, calling it to truce, while you are more deserving of Allah than they are, and Allah is with you.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾, he said: Do not be the first of the two groups to be struck down by its companion, ﴿while you are the superior﴾, he said: He says: while you are more deserving of Allah than they are.

Mention of those who said that the meaning of His saying ﴿while you are the superior﴾ is: you are the victorious, the more mighty than them.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿while you are the superior﴾, he said: The victorious, like the day of Uhud, when the reversal may be upon them.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior﴾, he said: This is abrogated. He said: It was abrogated by fighting and striving. He says: Do not be weak, you, and do not call them, you, to peace while you are the superior. He said: This was when there were treaties and truces between him and the polytheists, before fighting became obligatory. He says: Do not be weak and feeble, lest they see that you are calling to peace while you are above them and mightier than them. ﴿And you are the superior﴾: you are mightier than them. Then fighting came after that, and this abrogated it entirely, and He commanded them to strive against them and be harsh towards them. It has also been said: by His saying ﴿while you are the superior﴾ is meant: while you are the victorious in the end, even if they overcome you at some times and subdue you in some battles.

* *

And His saying ﴿So do not weaken﴾

It is in the jussive mood as a prohibition. In His saying ﴿and call﴾ there are two possibilities: the first is the jussive, as a conjunction with "do not weaken", so the meaning of the sentence is: do not weaken and do not call to peace; the second is the accusative, in the sense of a subordinate clause (ṣarf).

* *

And His saying ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾

It means: He will not wrong you in the rewards of your deeds, so that He diminishes their reward, from the saying of the Arabs: "wattara al-rajul" when you kill a slain man of his and then take his property by force.

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His saying ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, he says: He will not wrong you in the rewards of your deeds.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, he said: He will not diminish you.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾: that is, He will not wrong your deeds.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, likewise.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, he said: He will not wrong you; your deeds, that will not deprive you.

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, he said: He will not wrong your deeds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 36–37:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, the worldly life is but amusement and diversion. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.﴾ ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments.﴾

He, dhikruhu (may His remembrance be exalted), says: urging His believing servants to strive against His enemies, to spend in His cause, and to give up their lives in fighting the people of disbelief in Him: Fight, O believers, the enemies of Allah and your enemies from among the people of disbelief, and let not your desire for worldly life turn you away from fighting them, for the worldly life is only amusement and diversion, except for what in it is for Allah, such as deeds done in His cause and seeking His pleasure. As for everything other than that, it is only amusement and diversion, which vanishes and perishes and passes away, or it is sin that remains upon its owner, bringing him its shame and disgrace. ﴿And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards﴾: he says, if you act in this worldly life, the part of it that is not for it is amusement and diversion, and so you believe in Him and fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, and that is what remains for you of it, and it is not nullified by the length of amusement and play; then your Lord will give you your rewards for it, compensating you with something better for you than it on the day of your poverty and your need for your deeds. ﴿And He will not ask you for your wealth﴾: he says, your Lord will not ask you for your wealth, but He will charge you with His monotheism, rejecting what is other than Him of rivals, and devoting worship and obedience to Him alone. ﴿If He should ask it of you﴾: He, whose praise is exalted, says, if your Lord should ask you for your wealth, ﴿and press you﴾: he says, He would exert you with the request and insist upon you giving it, pressing you, ﴿you would be stingy﴾: he says, you would be stingy with it and withhold it from Him, out of your miserliness with it; but He knows that from you, and from the narrowness of your souls, so He did not ask you for it.

* *

And His words ﴿and He would bring out your resentments﴾

He says: and He, whose praise is exalted, if He asked you for your wealth by that request of His, would bring out your resentments. He said: Allah knows that in asking for wealth there is the bringing out of resentments.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Here you are, you who are called upon to spend in the way of God; but among you are some who are niggardly. Whoever is niggardly, is niggardly only toward himself. God is the Self-Sufficient, and you are the needy. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾ (47:38).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers: ﴿Here you are﴾, O people, ﴿you who are called upon to spend in the way of God﴾, meaning: you are called to spend in striving against the enemies of God and in support of His religion. ﴿But among you are some who are niggardly﴾ in spending for it. The particle "hā" has been introduced in two places, because when the Arabs wish to draw near (to indicate proximity), they place the pronoun between "hā" and "dhā," and they say: "hā anta dhā qā'iman" (here you are, standing). Since proximity is the response of speech, they sometimes repeat "hā" with "dhā," and sometimes they suffice with the first, omitting the second. They do not put "antum" before "hā," because "hā" is a response, so one does not draw near with it after the word.

And some of the grammarians of Basra said: the placing of the particle of attention in two places is for emphasis.

* *

And His words: ﴿Whoever is niggardly, is niggardly only toward himself﴾.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: whoever is niggardly in spending in the way of God, is niggardly only out of the niggardliness of his own soul, because if his soul were generous, it would not be niggardly in spending in the way of God, but would instead be liberal with it. ﴿God is the Self-Sufficient, and you are the needy﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God has no need, O people, of your wealth or your expenditures, because He is self-sufficient above His creation, and the creation is needy toward Him; you are of His creation, so you are needy toward Him. He urged you to spend in His way only so that He might gain for you, through that, a great reward from Him.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Here you are, you who are called upon to spend in the way of God; but among you are some who are niggardly. Whoever is niggardly, is niggardly only toward himself. God is the Self-Sufficient, and you are the needy﴾: He said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, has no need of you, and you are in greater need of Him.

And His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and if you turn away, O people, from this religion that Muhammad (ﷺ) has brought you, and you apostatize, turning back from it, ﴿He will replace you with another people﴾, meaning: He will destroy you, then bring other people besides you in your place, who will affirm it and act according to its laws. ﴿Then they will not be the likes of you﴾, meaning: then they will not be niggardly with what they have been commanded regarding spending in the way of God, nor will they neglect anything of the bounds of their religion, but they will fulfill all of that as they are commanded.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾: He said: if you turn away from My Book and My obedience, I will replace you with another people. By God, our Lord is able to do that, to destroy them, and to bring after them one who is better than them.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾: He said: if they turn away from obedience to God.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾ [[He did not give the interpretation here, being content with what precedes it as an indication of it, since the narration in the two hadiths is from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la.]].

It has been mentioned that by His words ﴿He will replace you with another people﴾ He meant: the non-Arabs of Persia.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Bazi' al-Baghdadi Abu Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Khalid, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "When the verse ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾ was revealed, Salman was beside the Messenger of God (ﷺ). They said: O Messenger of God, who are these people who, if we turn away, will be substituted for us? He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) struck Salman's shoulder and said: 'This man and his people. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if faith were suspended at the Pleiades, men from the people of Persia would attain it.'"

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid informed me, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited this verse ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾. They said: O Messenger of God, who are those who, if we turn away, will be substituted for us, and then will not be the likes of us? He struck the thigh of Salman and said: "This one and his people. And if faith were with the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it."

* Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Adani narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "This verse was revealed while Salman al-Farisi was beside the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his knee rubbing against his knee: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾. They said: O Messenger of God, and who are those who, if we turn away, will be substituted for us and then not be the likes of us? He struck the thigh of Salman and then said: 'This one and his people.'"

Mujahid said regarding this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿He will replace you with another people﴾: "whomever He wills."

Others said: they are the people of Yemen.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Rashid ibn Sa'd, Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr and Shurayh ibn Ubayd narrated to us, regarding ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you﴾: he said: the people of Yemen.
